passage:
Grandpa always kept an old pair of running shoes by the door. They were dirty and full of cracks.
His grandson asked why he did not throw them away.
Grandpa said those shoes were from the first race he ever finished. He was not fast, and many people passed him. But he had trained for months, and crossing the finish line changed how he saw himself.
The shoes were not useful anymore, but they reminded him that difficult things could be completed step by step.
His grandson looked at the shoes differently after that. They were not trash. They were a quiet trophy.
Some victories are not shown by gold medals. Sometimes they wait beside the door.
